title: Lucy Simpson:
title_q: “Look to Each Other for Our Strength”
title_short: Lucy Simpson · AYH · Look to Each Other for Our Strength
format: 9:16 only · 1080×1920 (the interview file is already vertical, 2160×3840)
headline: NIWRC's CEO, off the formal script: she is so very happy, she is grandma now, and her message to the world is to look to each other for our strength.
story: Warm and personal. Family first (“I'm grandma now, which is crazy”), then the work, arm in arm with other strong Native women leaders. She ends on community and resilience: NIWRC's voice in one line.
One clean AYH answer, in her order: yes, why, her message. B-roll is the reception: Native women together, talking. It shows “arm in arm” and “As Native people”. No harm on screen, no stock.

Loops: L1 “What is the source of her happiness?” opens at 0:03 and closes on “I'm grandma now” at 0:11. L2 “One message to the entire world?” opens at 0:20 and closes on “to the world” at 0:40. Stakes: Native resilience, shared with the world.
do: Let the “grandma” laugh play. It is the heart of the piece.
Use take 2 of the world message only (from 01:03.6).
Show Native women together on “arm in arm with so many other strong Native women leaders”.
Keep the same look as the Brandi, Christie and Cory AYH cuts: same top text, name super and caption style.
Close on her face for the last line.
dont: Do not use take 1 (“listen to the voices of our Native women”, 00:44.0 to 00:52.8) or “I don't know, let me think about that.”
Do not reuse bites from Ardit's Lucy cuts (“Safety Is Not the Absence of Violence”, “There Is No Shame in It”, donor thank-you). This clip shares none.
No B-roll woman who could be mistaken for Lucy (she wears a colorful patterned dress and beaded earrings).
No Tribal affiliation on the name super. No logo before the end card.

--- 26-10-09 C1 Happy - NIWRC Event 7.MP4 ---
[00:02.9] I am so very happy.
[00:10.1] My happiness comes from my family and my children and my grandchildren.
[00:14.4] I'm grandma now, which is crazy.
[00:17.8] And also just knowing that I do this work to promote safety in solidarity and arm in arm with so many other strong Native women leaders.
[00:38.4] [do not use, not an answer: I don't know, let me think about that.]
[00:44.0] [do not use, take 1: If I could give one message to the entire world, it would be to really listen to the voices of our Native women.]
[00:53.4] And if I could give one message to the entire world,
[01:03.6] it would be to really take care of each other, protect each other,
[01:09.2] and to look to each other for our strength.
[01:14.6] As Native people, we have so much resilience and it's just so important that we really have that opportunity to bring that knowledge and those experiences to the world.
[01:26.9] [do not use, crew talk: Good job. Okay.]
